name.name: Stomatal Development and Plant Interaction Regulator

description.text: This family of proteins is involved in diverse biological processes including development and interaction with symbiotic organisms. Members of this family play a crucial role in stomatal development, influencing cell fate progression, orientation of spacing divisions, and promoting asymmetric divisions in plant tissues. They are essential for the transition of meristemoids into guard mother cells and for regulating gene expression in differentiating cells. These proteins also form complexes with receptor kinases and are involved in the recognition of regulatory peptides, modulating ligand-receptor activity in developmental pathways. Additionally, some family members are implicated in growth promotion and seed production when interacting with endophytic fungi, suggesting a role in plant-microbe interactions.
